category_title: Older preschoolers using covert spaces and social exclusion for mischief
scenario_title: Covert play spaces and sophisticated social exclusion
minimal_context: Delia and Sarah are setting up a hidden play space behind the storage tables during morning free play.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Delia, Sarah, what are you two doing back here behind the storage tables with all those cushions?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Whispering to Sarah while cuddling together on the cushions) We are playing the Gymnastics Game. Pretend I am the coolest girl in town.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: I see. And how did the black wicker Teacher Chair get back here?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Nervously glances around to see if anyone is watching and secretes the chair further under the table) Sarah brought it. We need an exclusive space.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Well, Lizzie is walking over here now to see what you are playing. What should we say to her?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I’m so sorry, Lizzie, but only two are allowed in Gymnastics. The space is not big enough for three. I can tell you are feeling sad. Try again later.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Delia, Sarah, what are you two doing back here behind the storage tables with all those cushions?

STUDENT: (Whispering to Sarah while cuddling together on the cushions) We are playing the Gymnastics Game. Pretend I am the coolest girl in town.

TUTOR: I see. And how did the black wicker Teacher Chair get back here?

STUDENT: (Nervously glances around to see if anyone is watching and secretes the chair further under the table) Sarah brought it. We need an exclusive space.

TUTOR: Well, Lizzie is walking over here now to see what you are playing. What should we say to her?

STUDENT: I’m so sorry, Lizzie, but only two are allowed in Gymnastics. The space is not big enough for three. I can tell you are feeling sad. Try again later.

task.content: Establishing a private, hidden play space to play the 'Gymnastics Game', which requires creating an exclusive space and that a child play the role of an authentically Excluded Person.

context.environment: An unseen corner of the classroom not visible from common activity areas or the teacher's desk, behind storage tables.
context.materials: Couch cushions and pillows removed from window seats, tile floor, Joya's small black wicker Teacher Chair, an hourglass timer, plush hand-puppets.
context.social_setting: Morning free play period, cuddling together with bodies touching and whispering.
context.time_context: During the two-hour morning free play period.

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When another child attempts to join the game in the exclusive space.
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Uses a pseudo-official tone and the language of the 'Emotional Learning' curriculum to turn the other child away, legitimizing the exclusionary behavior.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Aware that one hard and fast rule of preschool is that 'You can't say you can't play', but intentionally navigating this to practice social exclusion.
related_quotes: I’m so sorry, Lizzie, but only two are allowed in Gymnastics. The space is not big enough for three
I’m sorry, but only two are allowed in this game right now. I can tell you are feeling sad. Try again later

behavior_patterns.condition: When setting up the game space and establishing the narrative.
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Quietly removes couch cushions and pillows without anyone noticing, directs peer to commit an act of brazen mischief by snatching the forbidden Teacher Chair, and secretes it under the storage table while nervously glancing around.
related_quotes: Pretend I am the coolest girl in town
